RYCKMAN, HON. EDMOND BAIRD, B.A., M.A., LL.B., K.C.—B. 1866; ed. Brantford Colleg. Inat., Toronto Univ. and Osgoode Hall; el. to H. of C., Canada, 1921; re-el., 1925; min. of pub. wkm. in Meighen Cabinet, 1926; re-el., g.e., 1926; min. of national rev. in Bennett cabinet, 1930.

RYRIE, MAJ.-GEN. HON. SIR GRANVILLE DE LAUNE, K.C.M.G. (1919), C.B. (1918), C.M.G. (1916), V.D.—B. 1865; ed. King's Schl., Parramatta; mem., state parl., N.S.W., 3 years, mem., house of reps., C. of A., 1911-27; asst. min. for defence, 1919-22; commanded 3rd Light Horse Regt., N.S.W., for 7 yrs. with rank of lieut.-col.; served S. Africa, 1900-01 (severely wounded (Queen's med. 4 claps)); European War, 1914-18; commanded 2nd Light Horse Brig., A.I.F., Egypt; commanded Australian divn., Syria; G.O.C., Australian Forces, Egypt (wounded twice, five times ment. in desps.); maj.-gen. commdg. 1st Cav. Divn., N.S.W., 1923-27; high commr. for Australia, 1927.

SADLER, C.—Asst. gen. man., govt. rly., Trinidad, Dec., 1914; traffic man., Nigerian govt. rly., Aug., 1922; gen. man., Trinidad govt. rly., Jan., 1926.

SAINT, SYDNEY JOHN, B.Se., A.I.C.—B.1897; ed. Beaminster Grammar Schl., Reading Univ.; B.Sc., 1920; served with R.A.F., 1916-19; Salters research fellow, 1920-22; lect. in agrl. chemistry, Leeds Univ., 1922-26; agrl. chemist, Barbados, 1927.

ST. JOHNSTON, LIEUT.-COL. SIR REGINALD, K.C.M.G. (1931), C.M.G. (1923). Barrister-at-law (Middle Temple); M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., Lond., etc.—Ed. Queen Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey and Cheltenham Coll.; various appts. in home civ. service; entered Fiji civ. serv., 1907; commnr. Lau Islands, 1909; seconded for European war; D.A.D.M.S., B.E.F., France; subsequently attached to W.O. (brevet lieut.-col. and reed. thanks of S. of S.); col. sec., Falkland Is., Dec., 1918; ag. gov., Falkland Is., from Sept. 1919 to Apr., 1920; col. sec., Leeward Islds., Dec., 1919; ag. gov., Leeward Is., eight times; admtd. govt. of Antigua on many occasions; ag. admstr., Dominica, 1925; admstr., St. Kitts-Nevis, 9th May, 1925; assumed duty, 23rd Nov., 1925; gov., Leeward Is., Sept., 1929; author of "The Lau Islands, Fiji," "The Children of the Sun," "The Falkland Islands," "The Islanders of the Pacific," "South Sea Reminiscences," "West Indian Tales" and some novels, etc.

SALIER, LIEUT.-COL. EDWARD LUCAS.—B. 1882; ed. Hutchins Schl., Hobart, Tasmania; 2nd lieut., 4th K.S.L.I., 1903; Northumberland Fusiliers, 1906; India, N.W. Frontier, 1908; seconded S. Nigeria Regt., W.A.F.F., 1910; asst. regtl. adjt., S.N. Regt., 1910; regtl. adjt., S.N. Regt., 1911-13; adjt., 3rd S.N. Regt., 1914; S.O., Fly and Cross River Columns, W.A.F.F., Cameroons, 1914; adjt., 2nd Northumberland Fusiliers, France, Belgium, Salonika, 1915; severely wounded, 1915; brig. major, 12th Australian Infy. Brig., France, Belgium, 1916-17; brevet major, June, 1917; G.S.O. II, Tank Corps, 1917; in commd., 1st Northumberland Fusiliers, 1918; G.S.O. I, Tank Corps, 1918; temp. lieut.-col., 1918; six times ment. in desps.; M.C., Legion of Honour, brevet major; in commd., 4th Nigeria Regt., W.A.F.F., 1920-21; Reg. Army, R. of O., Lieut.-Col., May, 1921; resigned, 31st Mar., 1925; contr., lab., Ascension Island (St. Helena Colony), Aug., 1925; pol. mag., offr. in ch., secretariat, ag. treas. and collr., cust. and clerk to exec. coun., St. Helena, May, 1928; govt. sec., Jan., 1929.

SALISBURY, THOMAS RONALD FPOULKEN.—B. 1882; served in Fiji, and under the condominium govt., New Hebrides; govt. agt., New Hebrides, 18th Mar., 1922.

SALMON, FREDERICK JOHN, M.C., A.C.G.I., F.R.G.S., Lieut.-Col., R. of O., R.E.—B. 1882; ed. Univ. Coll. Schl., Lond., and Cent. Tech. Coll., S. Kensington; emplo. on Transvaal Mines, 1904-1907; assoc., inst., of mining and metallurgy; asst. supt., surveys, Ceylon, June, 1908; supt., surveys, 1914; served with field survey units in France, 1915-19; thrice ment. in desps.; lieut.-co., supt., surveys, on staff (appl. surveys), Ceylon, 1924; ag. asst. surv.-gen. 1928; dir., land registr., and surveys, Cyprus, Sept., 1930.

SALOMONE, WALTER.—B. 1888; ed. St. Ignatius Coll. and Malta Univ.; elec. for 6th divn. in leg. assem., Oct., 1921; re-elec., June, 1924 and Aug., 1927; min. for industry and commerce, Aug., 1927.

SAMARAKOON, EDWIN RICHARD DE ALVEIS.—B. 1877; cls. V. Ceylon civ. serv., Oct., 1927; extra office asst., Badulla kach., Oct., 1927; office asst. to contr., rev., Feb., 1928; office asst. to land commnr., July, 1931.

SAMBIDGE, GERALD CHURCHILL.—B. 1886; ed. King Edward's Schl., Birmingham; served Nigeria Regt., Mar., 1915; instr. in arts and crafts, N. Provs., Nigeria, Dec., 1920.

SAMPSON, BASIL FEHRSSEN, M.C.—B. 1888; ed. St. Andrew's Coll., Grahamstown; M.B., B.S., Lond, Univ. (Guy's Hosp.), 1917; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1915; temp. surg., R.N. (H.M.S. Benbow), 1915; tempy. capt., S.A.M.C., France, 1916; M.C., 1918; asst. bacteriologist, Guy's Hosp.; senr. govt. pathologist, Union of S. Africa health dept., Durban, 1931.

SAMPSON, HON. HENRY WILLIAM—B. 1872; mem., Transvaal parlmt., 1907-10; mem., Union parlmt., 1910-29; O.B.E., 1918; joined Union cabinet as min. for posts and tele. and pub. wks., Nov., 1928; pres., S.A. typographical union, 1903-29.

SAMUEL, Rt. HON. SIR HERBERT LOUIS, P.C. (1908), G.B.E. (1920), M.A.—B. 1870; ed. University Coll. Schl. and Balliol Coll., Oxford; M.P., Cleveland Divn., N. Riding, Yorks., 1902-18; partly under sec., home dept., 1905-9; chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster (with a seat in the cabinet), 1909-10 and 1915-16; P.M.G., 1910-14 and 1915-16; pres. of the L.G.B., 1914-15; sec. of state for home affairs, 1916; chmn. of the select comte., of house of commons on national expenditure, 1917-18; British sp. commnr. to Belgium, 1919; grand offr. of the Order of Leopold of Belgium, 1919; high commnr., Palestine, 1920-25.
DOMINIONS OFFICE AND COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

SAMUEL, SILVERIO I., M.B.E. (1924).—Ed. at St. Gregory's Rom. Cath. gram. schl., Lagos; messr. and copyt., educ. off., Oct., 1897; clk. to inspr. of schls., Mar., 1899; sec. to comtes. for exhibtn. of schl. wks., 1902 and 1903; clk. and interpreter to trav. commr., Illeha, interior dept., Feb., 1904; 3rd cls. clk., gov'ts off., Aug., 1904; conf. clk. to the gov't of Nigeria.

SANDERS, JOHN OWEN, A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1892; ed. Elstow Schol. and Manchester Univ.; mil. ser., 1915-20; 2nd lieut., 1917; ag. capt., 1918; asst., Crewe loco. works, L.M.S.R., 1922; works man., F.M.S. Rly., 1924; run. supt., 1927; ag. traffic man., Aug., 1930.

SANDFORD, GEORGE RITCHIE, O.B.E. (1924), Barrister-at-Law, Inner Temple, 1924.—Asst. dist. commr., E. SANDFORD, THOMAS FREDERICK, M.B.E., B.A.—B. 1886; ed. Marlborough Coll. and Oriel Coll., Oxford; asst. native commr., N. Rhodesia, Sept., 1910; native commr., Apr., 1913; served in E. African campaign, 1915-19; ag. dist. commr., 1927; ag. prov. commr., in 1929, 1930 and 1931.

SANDS, WILLIAM NORMAN, F.L.S.—B. 1875; curator, botanic and experiment stations, Antigua, W. Indies, Sept., 1899; agrl. supt., St. Vincent, Mar., 1904; asst. economic botanist, agrl. dept., F.M.S., Jan., 1920; ag. economic botanist, various periods of 1921-1930; prin. agrl. offr., Kedah, July, 1930.

SANDYS, MELVILL KEVERNE TRELAWNY, M.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1890; on mil'y. serv., Aug., 1914; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Nov., 1919; attd., Ratnapura kach., Nov., 1919; office asst. to gov't. agt., N.W. Prov., Mar., 1922; ag. asst. gov't. agt., Puttalam, Oct., to Dec., 1922; ag. asst. gov't agt., Mullaitivu, July, 1923; dist. judge, Anuradhapura, July, 1925; pol. mag., Kurunegala, Oct., 1926; ag. agt., Hambantota, May, 1927; ag. dist. judge, Tangalla, June, 1927; asst. gov't. agt., Uva, July, 1927; ag. asst. gov't. agt., Matare, Aug., 1927; asst. settlmt., officer, Jan., 1929; asst. gov't. agt., Mannar, Nov., 1931.

SANGER-DAVIES, ARTHUR ELPHINSTONE.—B. 1885; ed. Dover Coll., Coopers Hill and Oxford (Diploma of Forestry, 1907); asst. conservator, forests, grade II., F.M.S. forest dept., 1907; grade I., 1912; dep. conservator, forests, 1919; ag. conserv., forests, S.S. and F.M.S., June, 1923; dep. conserv., forests, Oct., 1923; title of office changed to conserv., forests, Jan., 1930.

SANSON, CHARLES HENRY.—B. 1886; ed. Plymouth and Munnamed Coll.; barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1923; pol. probationer, 1906; regiar. of criminals, F.M.S. and S.S., 1910; asst. commr. of pol., Ipoh, 1911; adjt., F.M.S. pol., 1913; commr. of pol., Johore, 1921; sup't., pol., S'pore but cont. former appt., Nov., 1924; ch. pol. offr., S'pore, Dec., 1929; offg. ch. pol. offr., Perak, Nov., 1930.

SARAVANAMUTTU, P.—B. 1894; B.A., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., local divn., Aug., 1919; attd., Colombo, kach., Aug., 1919; ag. office asst. to gov't. agt., Kalutara, Feb., 1920; attd. to Matale Kach., June, 1920; addnl. dist. judge, Badulla, Mar., 1921; pol. mag., Dandagamuwa, Sept., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala, June, 1922; addnl. asst. gov't. agt., Colombo, Mar., 1923; addnl. asst. dir., educn., Dec., 1925; asst. gov't. agt., Mullaitivu, Dec., 1926; dist. judge, Kegalle, Mar., 1929; ag. asst. govt. agt., Hambantota, Mar., 1930.

SARGENT, CAPT. R. G., M.B.E. (1928), A.I.N.A., F.R.G.S.—Port. offr., Kenya, Jan., 1917; port capt., 1925.

SARGENT, JOHN DENYS, B.A. (Oxon.), Dipl., Forestry, Oxford.—B. 1888; asst. conserv., forests, Ceylon, Dec., 1909; dep. conserv., grade II., Apr., 1917; grade I., May, 1919; conserv., Sept., 1921.

SARGENT, THOMAS PERCIVAL.—B. 1882; jr. asst. engr., constrn. dept., F.M.S.R., Aug., 1908; asst. engr. ocnstrn. dept., Sept., 1911; dist. engr., III., Sept., 1915; dist. engr., grade I., Jan., 1921; attd. head office, Sept., 1925.

SAUNDERS, Sir CHARLES JAMES RENAULT, K.C.M.G., 1906. C.M.G., 1896.—B. 1867; held various appts. in Natal civ. ser., 1876-87, when he ratified treaty with Queen of Amatongaland (despe.); res. mag., Eshowe, and J.P. for Zululand, 1888; defined bndry. between Amatongaland and Zululand, 1889 (despe.); variously employed under Zululand Gov't., 1888-96 (despe.), when he was apptd. spec. commr. for Trans-Pongoland territory, carried out final act of annexation of that territory and declared British prot. for Amatongaland; acted as res. commr. and chief mag. of Zululand, 1896; apptd. chief mag. and civ. commr. for prov. of Zululand on its incorporation with Natal, 1897; medal, S. African War, 1899-1902; col. representative on Zululand Lands Delimitation Com., 1902, and commr. for native affairs, 1905; ret., 1909.

SAUNDERS-JONES, DAVID WILLOUGHBY.—B. 1899; ed. Christ Coll., Brecon; Indian Army, 1917-23; on service in Waziristan, Egypt and Palestine; wounded in Palestine, 1919; asst. dist. commr., Zanzibar, Feb., 1924; pvtc. sec., Br. res., June to Dec., 1925; ag. prov. commr., Pemba, June, 1930; ag. pvtc. sec. to Br. res., Aug., 1930.

SAUVE, HON. ARTHUR, P.C. (Can.).—B. 1875; ed. Seminary of Ste. Therese and l'Univ. de Montreal; lst cl. to legis. assem., Quebec, g.e., 1908; re-elec., g.e., 1912, 1916, 1919, 1923 and 1927; el. to H. of C., Canada, g.e., 1930; P.M.G., in Bennett Cabinet, 1930; re-elec. by accl. after assuming office, Aug., 1930.

SAVAGE, GEORGE.—B. 1887; aspt. of regtn., G.P.O., Singapore, Oct., 1914; aspt. of mails, ditto, Jan., 1915; sup't. mails, Penang, but cont. ag. senr. sup't. mails, July, 1917; sup't., grade II., Jan., 1919; sup't., grade I., Jan., 1920; sup't., posts and tels., Malacca, Sept., 1920; senr. acct., G.P.O., S'pore, contd. to act as contr., P. and T., Jan., 1929; contr., P. and T., F.M.S., Aug., 1929; ag. P.M.G., Sept., 1929; P.M.G., Johore, July, 1930.

SAVARY, JOHN LEWIS HENRY WILLIAM.—B. 1884; col. schol., Trinidad, 1901; Gray's Inn, 1902; prizeman in evidence, procedure and criminal law exam., 1904; barrister-at-law, Nov., 1905; practised at bar, Trinidad, 1906-24; retainer from Trinidad govt. as junr. coun. to atty.-gen., Jan., 1916-Dec., 1923; ag. solr.-gen., in 1921, 1922 and 1923; regiar. and marshal and regiar.-gen. and prin. regiar., West Indian ct. of appeal, Jan., 1929; ag. puisne judge in 1926 and 1926; puisne judge, Br. Guiana, 1928.

SAVI, VICTOR GEORGE.—B. 1884; pol. probationer, S.S., Nov., 1904; asst. sup't pol., Jan., 1908; asst. sup't. of pol., Penang, Oct., 1917; dir., crim. intell., Jan., 1920; dep. commr., pol., Perak, Mar., 1922; sup't. pol., S'pore, 1932.
SAWARD, CAPT. SIDNEY CARMON, M.C. (1916), M.M. (1916).—B. 1889; fellow of surveyors' inst.; served with 509 (1-1) Lond. Field Coy., R.E., 6th divn.; home serv., Aug. to Dec., 1914; France and Germany, Dec., 1914 to June, 1919; Ireland, June to Aug., 1919; commdg., cadre, 12th Field Co., R.E.; comand., Sept., 1918; lieut., June, 1916; capt., Oct., 1918; ag. major, Dec., 1918 to Jan., 1919; ment. in despa., Mar., 1919; survr., Gold Coast, Nov., 1919; field supervisor Apr., 1924; ag. dep. survr.-gen. on various occasions, 1925-30; ag. survr.-gen., Feb.-June, 1927; asst. survr.-gen., Apr., 1929.

SAWREY-COOKSON, SYDNEY SPENCER, B.A.—B. 1876; ed. Uppingham and New Coll., Oxford; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1903; judicial comsnr., N. Borneo, 1910-20; compiler, revd. edn., N. Borneo laws; judge, sup. ct., Gambia, 1920; compiler, revd. edn. (1926) Gambia laws; puisne judge, Gold Coast, 11th June, 1925.

SAWTELL, WILLIAM GEORGE.—B. 1894; ed. at King Edward VII's Sch., Bath, and H.M.S. "Worcester"; H.M. Transport Serv., 1915-17; Indian gov't. tel. ship, 1917-18; Indian Army R. of O., 1918-22; wharf-mast. and pilot, Tanganyika Territory, 1922.

SAXTON, SIDNEY WARING.—Ed. Toulouse (France), and Dean Close Schl., Cheltenham; paymr. cadet, R.N., July, 1906; paymr.-lieut.-comdr., Mar., 1918; 1st cls. French interpreter, lent to C.O. and apptd. asst. dist. comsnr., G. Coast, Sept., 1914, but did not take up apptnt., having resumed duty in H.M. Navy for the period of the war; assumed duties as junr. asst. col. sec., G. Coast, Apr., 1919; ag. asst. col. sec., May, 1919; ag. dist. comsnr., Accra, and ag. trav. comsnr. for Accra-Akwapim and Birrim dists., Oct., 1919; invalided, H.M. Navy, 1920; passed Tropical African service course (all subjects, 2nd part); barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1925; promoted pay commdr., ret. list, 1927; dep. prov. comsnr., 1930.

SAYER, GEOFFREY ROBLET, B.A.—B. 1887; ed. at Highgate schl. (foundationer) and Queen's Coll., Oxford; open exhib. in classics and Fitzgerald exhib.; 2nd ols. class. mods.; 3rd cls. lit. hum. (B.A., 1910); cadet, Hong Kong, Oct., 1910; passed in Cantonese, Nov., 1912; ag. asst. dist. offr. (South), 1912 to 1913; ag. asst. supt. pol., 1913 to 1914; ag. dep. offr. recvr., 1914 to 1915; ag. ch. asst. sec. for Chinese affrs. 1914 and 1915, in addn. to other duties; priv. sec. to gov., in addn. 1916; attd. to crown sol'r's off., 1915; passed final exam. in Hakka, July, 1915; ag. chief asst. sec. for Chinese affrs., 1915; on mily. serv., 1915-19; dep. regis. and appraiser, Hong Kong, 1920; head, sany. dept., 1920; passed in Mandarin, May, 1921; attd. to treasury, 1924; asst. treas. and comsnr. of estate duties, Apr., 1925; supt. impts. and expts. dept., June, 1927; P.M.G., Apr., 1928; head, sany. dept., Oct., 1928.

SAYERS, ELDERD FRANK.—B. 1889; ed. King's Coll. Schl., Wimbledon, St. John's Coll., Cambridge, and Grenoble Univ., B.A., LL.B. (Cantab.); barrister-at-law (Inner Temple), Apr., 1913; passed lower and higher stand. exams. in Temne, and lower stand. exam. in Koranko; war service, E. Africa, 1918; asst. dist. comsnr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1915; dist. comsnr., Aug., 1922.

SAYERS, FREDERICK RICHARDSON.—M.D., D.P.H., Dublin Univ.; ed. Rathmines Schl., Dublin, The Meath Hosp., Dublin, and Trin. Coll., Dublin; res. med. offr., Monkstown Hosp., Dublin, 1909-12; med. offr., S.S., Mar., 1912; med. offr., gen. hosp., Penang, Apr., 1912; med. offr., dist. hosp., Penang, 2nd June, 1912; port health offr. SCHARFF, JOHN WILLIAM, B.A., M.D., B.A.O., B.Ch., D.P.H. (T.C.D.), D.T.M. & H. SCHMIDT, CARL FRIEDRICH, B.A.—Civ. serv. law clk., law dept., Cape May, 1893; control and audit office, July, 1893; asst. examnr. of accts., Jan., 1894; examnr., May, 1896; ch. examnr., July, 1907; inspr. of accts., Jan., 1909; prin. clk., Apr., 1912; sec., educn. dept., Bloemfontein, 16th Aug., 1915; ag. dir. of educn., O.F.S., July, 1918; dir. of educn., O.F.S., June, 1920; sec. for interior, Sept., 1926; contr. and audr.-gen., 1929.

SCOTLAND, Douglas William, F.S.I., N.D.A., N.D.D., H.A.A.C. Dip.—Ed. at Mussoorie Schl., India and Alleynes Schl., Stone, Staffs.; Agric. SCOTLAND, Erica Eleanor.—Ent. C.O. as typist, July, 1913; shorthand writer, Aug., 1918; cler. offr., 9th Mar., 1922.

Fell. of Royal Soc. of medicine; Fell. of Royal Inst. of preventive medicine; Fell. of Soc. of tropical medicine and hygiene.—Ed. at St. Bart's and St. Thomas's hosps.; Univ. Colls. SEYMOUR-HALL, CHARLES CYRIL WILLIAM, F.R.S.A., F.R.G.S., F.R. Met. SHARP, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B. 1888; ed. Univ. Coll. Schl. and King's Coll., London; compt. and acct.-gen.'s dept., G.P.O., 1907-12; acct., postal dept., S. SHARPE, SIR ALFRED, K.C.M.G. (1903), C.B. SHARPE, H.—Asst. dist. commr., Kenya Colony, Apl., 1919; ag. dist. commr., 1926.

SHAW, JOHN HENRY DE BURGH, B.L.—B. 1887; ed. Clifton Schl., Dalkey, Dublin and Corrig Schl., Kingston; asst. dist. commr., Sierra Leone, May, 1921; dist. commr., May, 1928.

SHEEDY, CAPT. FREDERICK JOHN, M.B.E., B.Sc., M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1886; ed. SHELLEY, MALCOLM BOND.—B. 1879; ed. SHELSWELL-WHITE, GEOFFREY HENRY.—Barrister-at-Law.—B. 1897; ed. Off. Gaz., 1931.

SHELTON, C. F., M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.D. (Lond.), B.S.—Civil surgeon. Serbian red cross, 1913; surgeon lieut., 1914-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Sept., 1921.

SHEPPARD, CHARLES HENRY, M.B.E.—B. 1897; European War, 1914-1918; ment. in desps.; Kurdish gendarmerie, 1919-21; inspecting offr., Iraq pol., 1922-31; asst. commndt., pol., Somaliland, 1931.

SHELTON, JAMES, F.I.C.—B. 1886; asst. rech. and analytical chem. in the sc. and tech. dept., Imp. Inst., G. Britain, Mar., 1909; 2nd asst. govt. analyst, Singapore, Feb., 1915; chem. geolog. dept., F.M.S., Feb., 1917; in charge, of geolog. dept., June, 1917; on sp. duty at Inst. Med. SIDLEY, HON. SIR THOMAS KAY, KT, B.A. (1930), B.A., LL.B.—B. 1863; ed. pvt. schls., Otago Boys' High Schl., and Otago Univ., N.Z.; barrister and solr., 1889; mem., N.Z. H. of R., 1901-28; atty.-gen. and leader of legis. coun., 1928; also min. of just., 1929-30.

SIDLEY, WILLIAM HENRY FRANCIS, B.A. (Trinity Coll., Dublin).—Cadet, R.I.C., Aug., 1908; 3rd cls. dist. inspr., Oct., 1908; 2nd cls., Feb., 1910; 1st cls., Aug., 1919; couzty inspr., Nov., 1920; served in R.I.C. until disbandment of that force, July, 1922; depot inspr. SILVA, POPTHOWGE OSMUND SAMUEL EDERESINGHE, B.A. (Lond.)—B. 1904; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Feb., 1927; attd., Puttalam kach., Mar., 1927; attd., Kalutara kach., Dec., 1927; ag. pol. mag., Kalutara, Nov., 1928; office asst., Anuradhapura kach., Aug., 1929.

SMITH, ROBERT EDMUND, B.A. (Cantab.)—B. 1881; ast. mast., Outram Rd. Schl., Singapore, Aug., 1906; ditto, Raffles Inst., Nov., 1907, July, 1912, and Oct., 1913; headmast., Victoria Bridge Schl., Singapore, Mar., 1922.

SMITH, SIDNEY W.—B. 1902; apptd., after compet. exam., ast. clk., C.O., Oct., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; ag. higher grade cler. offr., 29th Oct., 1930.

SMITH, STEPHEN HENRY, C.B.E. (1929), F.R. Aus. H.S.—B. 1885; ed. Grafton Superior Pub. Sch.; inspr., continuation schl., N. S. Wales, June, 1912 to Feb., 1920; ast. under sec., educn. dept., N.S.W., June, 1920; dir., educn., N.S.W., 1923.

SMITH, STEPHEN JOHN.—B. 1887; N.Z. post and tel. dept., 1903; internal affrs. dept., 1913; sec., Samoan admstrn., 1915; ch. clk., external affrs. dept., 1920-30; ch. clk., Cook Is. dept., 1920-28; sec., 1928.

SMITH, HON. SYDNEY GEORGE.—B. 1879; ed. public schl., New Plymouth, N.Z.; mem., N.Z. house of reps., 1918-26 and since 1928; chmn., comtees., 1928; min., lab. and immigrn., 1930.

SMITH, WALTER JOHN.—B. 1884; ast. supt. wks., P.W.D., S. Stltms., Jan., 1908; ast. engnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Sept., 1909; ex. engnr., Kedah, Apr., 1917; ex. engnr., grade III, July, 1908; sen. ex. engnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Aug., 1923; ag. state engnr., Pahang, Jan., 1930.

SMITH, WILLIAM HARDEN, B.A., M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O. (T.C.D.), L.M. (Rot.), D.P.H. (R.C.P. and S.I.), D.T.M. (Calculta).—ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; surg. sub-lieut., R.N.V.R., 1918; med. offr., Zanzibar, Nov., 1925; ag. D.D.S.S., May to Sept., 1930 and June to Dec., 1931.

SMITH, WILLIAM HUMPHREY.—B. 1878; ed. Uppingham and Jesus Coll., Camb., Rustat schol., 1897; Abbott univ., schol., 1899; B.A., 1st cls., classic tripus, pt. I, 1901; 2nd cls. pt. II, history, 1902; clk., col. audit branch, exchequer and audit dept., Dec., 1903; ast. audr., Nyasaland, Oct., 1904; audr., N. Nigeria, Feb., 1910; examr., exchequer and audit dept., Aug., 1910; audr., Seychelles, Mar., 1911; 1st divn. clk. (2nd cls.), col. audit dept., Oct., 1912; on mil. serv., Aug., 1914; capt., K.O.Y.L.I., Jan., 1915; wounded, Mar., 1917; relinquished comm. owing to wounds, and returned to col. audit dept., Sept., 1918; audr., Uganda, Dec., 1923; audr., Kenya, 1927.

SMITH, WILLIAM RAMSAY.—D.Sc., M.D., M.S., Edin.; chmn. cent. bd. of health, coroner, vaccination offr., and inspr. of anatomy, S. Australia, 1899-1903; chmn., cent. bd. of health and coroner, 1903-29; author of several medical and scientific works.

SMUTS, GEN. THE RIGHT HON. J. C., P.C. (1917), C.H., K.C., B. 1870; ed. at Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; B.A., Cape Univ., 1891; Ebben scholar at Christ's Coll., Camb.; double first in law tripus, 1894; barrister, Cape Col.; state-attorney, S. African Republic, 1898; served with Boer forces during S. African war, and was in cmd. of Boer forces in Cape Col. during the latter part of the campaign; mem. of head comtees. of Het Volk : col. sec., Transvaal, 1907; mem. of Imp. Conf. on Naval and Military Defence, 1909; min. of finance and defence, Union of S. Africa, 1912; min. of defence, 1915; in command of troops in E. Africa, 1916; mem. of British war cabinet; represented S. Africa at peace confere. at Paris, 1919; prime min. and min. of native affrs., Union of S. Africa, 1919-24; M.P. for Standerton, 1924.

SMYLY, SIR PHILIP CRAMPTON, KT. BACH., (1905).—B. 1866; ed. at Trin. Coll., Dub., B.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, King's Inn, Dub., 1883; LL.D., 1891; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1902; Queen's advocr., S. Leone, 1896; atty.-gen., 1896; ch. just., S. Leone, 1901; ch. just., Gold Coast, 1911; ret., 1929.

SNELGAR, HERBERT JOHN.—B. 1890; ed. Christ's Hosp. and Kings Coll., London; clk., td. of educn., 1906; clk., C.A., 1910; clk., land dept., E.A.P., 1912; ag. office supt., 1917 and 1919; land ast., 1919; sec., land tenure comm., 1920; warden of mines, 1920; regiar. of titles, etc., 1922; ast. land offr., 1922.

SNEILL, EDWARD WALTER.—B. 1879; ast., post office, Kingwilliamstown, Mar., 1900; ast., G.P.O., Cape Town, Nov., 1900; clk., accs. branch, July, 1903; 1st cls. clk., Apl., 1912; income tax office, Pretoria, Sept., 1914; senr. clk., income tax office, Cape Town, July, 1915; senior clk., rev. office, Johannesburg, Mar., 1918; prin. clk., ditto, Jan., 1921; ch. clk., income tax, head office, inland rev. dept., Pretoria, Aug., 1921; ast. comsrr. inland rev., Sept., 1929.

SOLLIS, CLIFFORD GEORGE, B.A.—B. 1895; ast. mast., Bukit Zahrah Sch., Johore Bahru, Dec., 1920; ag. inspr., schls., Pahang, Oct., 1925; supt., educn., Kedah, Dec., 1930.

SOLOMON, MICHAEL CLAUDE.—Copyist, med. dept., Jamaica, Oct., 1885; 3rd cls. clk., 1888; 2nd cls. clk., 1891; 1st cls. clk. and sec., cent. bd. of health, 1908; ch. clk., 1920; sec. to comm. on reorganization of med. serv., 1920.
SOLOMON, Neville Stafford Victor.—B. 1874; clk., G.F.O., Bahamas, 1891; tel. dept., 1892; treas. and cust., 1895; supervisor, cust., 1896; gold gde., Gold Coast, 1902; ag. ch. reg., sup. ct., 1906; finan. ast., treas. and cust. dept., Nigeria, 1907; supervisor, 1st gde., cust. dept., 1910; collr., 1917; adm. reporting offr., various ports, Nigeria, during great war, 1914-18; ret. on pension, 1922; ast. postmr. (temp.), Bahamas, Jan., 1924; resigned, Nov., 1925; recr. gen. and treas., and mem. exec. coun., Bahamas, 1928; mem., leg. coun., Feb., 1931; chmn., licensing authority, Mar., 1931; has held various ag. appts.

SOLOMON, Saul.—B. 1875; ed. Bedford Grammar Schl. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; M.A.; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1900; K.C., Union of S. Africa, 1919; judge, sup. ct., Transvaal prov. divn., 1927.

SOMASUNTHARAM, Kandiah.—B. 1897; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; attd., Kalutara kach., Dec., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala kach., Jan., 1922; ditto, Colombo Kach., Dec., 1922; office ast., rubber contr., Mar., 1923; office ast., Galle kach., Aug., 1926; 5th ast. col. sec., Nov., 1926; 4th ast. col. sec., May, 1928; addnl. ast. govt. agt., Colombo, Jan., 1929; addnl. ast. contr., rev., Nov., 1929.

SOMERS (6th Baron, cr. 1784), Arthur Herbert Somers Cocks, K.C.M.G. (1926), D.S.O. (1919), M.C. (1917).—B. 1887; ed. Charterhouse and New Coll., Oxford; serv. in Great War, 1914-19; capt., 1st Life Guards, 1914; lieut.-col., Tank Corps, 1918-19; ret., 1922; a lord in waiting in ordinary to the King, 1924; gov'r. of Victoria, 1926-31.

SOMERS, Cecil George.—B. 1896; served Dardanelles and E. Mediterranean with H.M. Transporta, 1914-18; gov't. pilot, Kenya, 1924; ast. port offr., Zanzibar, 1929; ag. port offr., Aug., 1929 to Mar., 1930.

SOMMERVILLE, James, O.B.E.—Ck., traffic dept., Cape, 20th Mar., 1897; clk., C.T. M. office, Cape, 1st Oct., 1898; ch. clk., admtr.'s office, Transvaal, 1st Dec., 1900; sec., refugees aid dept., 1st Nov., 1901; sec., Transvaal immigr. office, 1st Aug., 1903; ch. clk., lands dept., 1st May, 1904; under sec. for lands, Union of Africa, 1st June, 1917; sec. for lands, 1st Apr., 1921.

SOPER, John Robert Philpott, B.A. (hons.), Cantab.—B. 1904; ed. Tonbridge Schl. and Pembroke Coll., Cambridge (schol.); head-master, agril. prim. schl., Zanzibar, Sept., 1926; seconded for duty as agril. offr., Nov., 1926; agril. offr., Jan., 1928.

SOUTH, Francis Wilton, M.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1886; mycologist and lect. in agril. sci., Imp. dept. of agr. for W. Indies, Mar., 1909; ch. agril. instr., agril. dept., F.M.S., May, 1913; ch. agril. field offr., Nov., 1924; ag. sec. for agril., S.S. and F.M.S., for various periods 1927-31; rep. of Malaya at mycological confce. in Lond., Sept., 1929.

SOUTHBOROUGH, 1st Baron (creat. 1917), Rt. Hon. Sir Francis John Stephens Hopwood, P.C. (1912), G.C.B. (1916), G.C.M.G. (1908), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1906), C.B. (1895), C.M.G. (1883).—B. 1860; ed. at Louth by Canon W. W. Hopwood; admitted a solr., 1882; ast. law clk., B. of T., 1885-1888; ast. astor., 1888-1892; priv. sec. to pres. of B. of T., 1892; sec., rly. dept., 1892-1901; perm. sec., 1901; perm. under-sec. of S. for the colonies, 1907-1910; employed on different occasions upon offl. missions to U.S.A., Canada, and Newfoundland; Brit. deleg. to internat. rly. congress in London, 1896; and in Paris, 1900; hon. sec. to chmn. of select comte. of H. of C. on Jameson raid, 1897; mem. of London traffic coman., 1903; visited S. Africa as mem. of Transvaal and O.R.C. constitutions coman., 1906; mem. of coman. on canals and waterways, 1906; and on ocean freights and shipping "rings," 1906; accompanied H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit to Quebec, 1908; mem. of Royal coman. on electoral reform, 1909; regiar. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1907-1909; sec. of the Order, 1909-1911; accompanied H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught on his visit to S. Africa in connection with the opening of the first parlmt. of the Union of S. Africa, 1910; vice-chmn. of the Development coman., 1910; specially apptd. to act as under sec. of state for the colonies during the period of the Imperial Conf., 1911; additional civil lord of the Admiralty, Jan., 1912; sec. to the Irish Convention, 1917.

SOUTHORN, Wilfrid Thomas, C.M.G. (1927).—B. 1879; ed. Warwick schl. and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1903; off. ast. to govt. agt., N. Prov., Oct. 1904; N.C. Prov., May, 1905; dist. judge, Tangalla, Apr., 1907; landing survr., customs, Colombo, July, 1909; ast. govt. agt., Matale, Nov., 1911; priv. sec. to govt., Aug., 1914; dep. collr. of customs and landing survr., Colombo, Sept., 1915; 2nd ast. col. sec., Dec., 1919; priv. ast. col. sec., July, 1920; prin. collr., cust. and chmn., Colombo port coman., Dec., 1923; mem., leg. coun., 1924 and exec. coun., 1925; col. sec., Hong Kong, May, 1926; O.A.G., in 1927, 1928, 1929 and 1930.

SPARROW, William La Bart.—B. 1904; pol. probationer, Nov., 1924; ast. supt. pol., 1927; seconded to Weihaiei as junr. dist. offr., Jan., 1928; passed in Mandarin, 1931.

SPEARMAN, Barugh, M.A., M.B., B.C. (Camb.), D.T.M. and H., certif., London Schl. of Trop. Medicine (with distinction).—B. 1877; med. offr., Uganda Prot., Sept., 1912; capt., Uganda med. serv., Sept., 1916; med. offr. of hth., Zanzibar, Nov., 1920; read. thanks of ag. gov., Uganda, for services in connection with outbreak of plague at Jinja, Nov., 1914; ment. in desps., 1919; M.O.H., Zanzibar, Sept., 1920; senr. med. offr. of health, Zanzibar, Jan., 1923; ag. D.M.S.S., on various occasions, 1922-23, 1925-26, 1928 and 1930; D.D.S.S., Jan., 1926; 3rd cls., Order of Brilliant Star of Zanzibar, 1929.

SPEED, Sir Edwin Arney, K.T. Bach. (1911).—M.A., LL.B.; B. 1869; ed. at Rugby, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; major scholar and senior exhibtnr., Rugby schl.; scholar and prizeman of Trin. Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. class. tripes, 1890; 2nd cls. law tripes, Part I., 1891; called to the bar, Inner Temple, June, 1893; dist. coman., G. Coast, 1899; atty.-gen., Lagos, 1900; edited a revised edition of Lagos laws, 1901; has acted on numerous occasions as ch. just. and also as col. sec., from Jan., 1905, to Mar., 1906; atty.-gen., S. Nigeria, May, 1906; edited revised edtn. of laws of S. Nigeria, 1907; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1908; retired.

SPENCER, Cyril Edward.—B. 1873; entd. col. ser., Cyprus, 1st Mar., 1891; in secretariat from Apr., 1892 to May, 1898; also clk. to legis. coun., Mar., 1894, to May, 1898; priv. sec. to high coman. on several occasions, 1898-1900; inspr., mil. pol., 1st May, 1898; ag. dist. comdt., July, 1900, to Jan., 1904; apptd. in com. of diva. of pol., Jan., 1904; also gov. of pris. and asst. to dist. coman., and dep. coroner; ag. dist.
DOMINIONS OFFICE AND COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

conmr., Apr. to Dec., 1905; passed in mod. Greek, higher standard, 1904; and in Turkish, lower standard, 1906; transf. to B. East Africa, as ast. dist. conmr., Nov., 1906; ag. supt., inland rev., Apr. to Oct., 1907; ag. dist. conmr., Mombasa, from July, 1907; dist. conmr., E.A.F., Apr., 1912; senr. ast. sec., secretariat, Jan., 1919; elk. of councils, Jan., 1919; ag. ast. chief sec., Jan., 1919; commr. of prisons, Kenya, Oct., 1923.

SPICER, ROY GODFREY BULLEN, M.C. (1918).—B. 1889; ed. Colet Court and St. Paul's; probationary ast. supt. pol., Ceylon, Nov., 1909; ast. supt., 1911; sup't., 1915; on war serv., 1915-19; wounded, Oct., 1918; returned to Ceylon pol., 1919; supt., grade I, 1923; commr. pol., Kenya, June, 1926; comdt., pol., Palestine, 1930.

SPILLER, JOHN WYATT, M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1878; ed. Wellington Schol. (Som.); served in engrg. dept., G.W.R., 1896 to 1910; joined engrg. dept., Crown Agents, 1910; services lent to Miny. of Munitions, 1916; tech. adviser to dir. Munitions Overseas Transport, 1917; returned to C.A., 1919; dep. ch. engrg., 1919; visited Ceylon, F.M.S. and S. Stlmta, 1920; ch. engrg. (designs), 1922; visited Br. Guiana and Trinidad, 1922; acted for one year as gen. man., F.M.S. rly., and ch. engrg., 1926.

SPIO-GABRRAH, JOSEPH.—B. 1878; 2nd ast. mast., tech. schl., Accra, Gold Coast, Jan., 1899; 1st ast. mast., Nov., 1902; 3rd grade teacher, Jan., 1907; prin. teacher, Nov., 1912; ast. headmast., Apr., 1920; headmast., Apr., 1922; insp., schls., Apr., 1923.

SPOONER, MAJOR JOHN CHARLES GARTE, M.C.—B. 1883; ed. Marlborough Coll.; jr. ast. engrg., F.M.S. rly., 1903-06; ast. engrg., F.M.S. rly., 1906-12; dist. engrg., grade III, 1912-14; dist. engrg., grade II, 1914; on active serv., 1915-19; dist. engrg., grade I, Ipoh, Jan., 1920; sen. dist. engrg., Ipoh, Jan., 1921; senr. dist. engrg., Johore Bahru, Mar., 1927; ditto, Kuala Lumpur, Nov., 1928; engrg., ways and wks., June, 1929.

SPOWERS, JAMES HOWARD.—B. 1889; authorised surv., Queensland, Oct., 1911; surv., F.M.S., Nov., 1913; ast. supt., surveys, Jan., 1919; ast. supt., trig. surveys, F.M.S., Nov., 1922; ast. supt., rev. surveys, Sept., 1924; ag. sr. ast. supt., surveys, Singapore, Apr., 1930.

SPRING, FREDERICK GEORGE, N.D.A., U.D.A., F.L.S.—B. 1887; supt., govt. plantations, F.M.S., Sept., 1910; agriculturist, agrl. dept., May, 1912; agriculturist (rubber), Jan., 1926; sec. to co-op. societies dept., May, 1927.

SPROULE, PERCY JULIAN, B.A., Camb.—B. 1873; barrister-at-law (Mid.Tem.); cadet, S.S., Nov., 1895; dep. regis., sup. ct., Penang, Sept., 1899; dep. pub. prosecutor, Sing., Aug., 1906; solr.-gen., Apr., 1911 and May and Oct., 1912; puisne judge, Dec., 1913; pres., toddy comm., Selangor, Oct., 1916; senr. puisne judge, Feb., Apr., 1921, Oct., 1926 and Apr., 1928; ag. ch. judl. commr., F.M.S., June, 1924; ag. ch. just., S.S., Apr., 1925, Mar., 1928 and in 1931.

SQUIRE, REV. CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1888; ed. Repton and Trinity Coll., Cambridge (B.A.); supt. educ., S. Prova., Nigeria, 1927; ag. prin., King's Coll., Lagos, 1928; prin., govt. coll., Ibadan, 1928.

STAGE, WALTER TERENCE.—B.A., Trin. coll., Dublin; B. 1886; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 29th Oct., 1910; attached to the Galle kachcheri, 1st Dec., 1910; office ast. to govt. agt., Galle, March, 1912; pol. mag., Chilaw, May, 1913; pol. mag., Gampola, Feb., 1914; ag. pol. mag., Kandy, May, 1915; priv. sec. to gov. and extra ast. col. sec., Sept., 1915; ast. censor, Dec., 1916; censor, May, 1918; dist. judge, Negombo, Apr., 1920; ast. stimt. offr., Jan., 1922; ag. stimt. offr., Mar.-Nov., 1926; mayor of Colombo, Oct., 1927 to June, 1928; ag. contr., rev., Apr., 1931; ch. munie. coun. and mayor, Colombo, July, 1931.

STAFFORD, FRANK EDMUND.—B. 1886; ed. R. Grammar Schl., Guildford; Queen's Regt., 1914-19; joined 'Iraq civil adminstr., Feb., 1919; ag. ast. rev. sec., Oct., 1919; supervising offr. high commn., Oct., 1920; ast. to finan. adviser to high commn., June, 1921; dep. fin. sec. to high commn., Jan., 1923; ag. finan. sec., Apr., 1923; finan. sec., June, 1923.

STAINES, CAPT. EDMUND ALFRED.—B. 1882; P. and T. dept., G. Britain, 1899; Br. sea post offr., U.K.-U.S.A., 1907; ast. supt., P. and T., F.M.S., Sept., 1911; mil. service, 1915-18; ag. acct., P. and T., F.M.S., 1921-25; contrlr., P. and T., Perak and Dindings, June, 1927; ditto, Selangor and Pahang, June, 1928.

STALLWORTHY, HON. ARTHUR JOHN.—B. 1877; ed. State schl., N.Z.; entd. N.Z. parl., 1928; min. of health, 1928.

STANFORD, COL. THE HON. SIR WALTER ERNEST MONTMIRER, K.B.E. (1919), C.B. (1901), C.M.G. (1892), O.B.E. (1918).—B. 1860; mag.'s clk., Cape Col., 1863; mag., 1876; capt. of levies in Goaleka war, 1877-8 (medal and clasp); mem. native laws and customs comm., 1880-2; comdt. in war of 1880-1 (med. and clasp); on special service to Pondoland, 1884; ch. mag. Griqualand E., 1885; negotiated treaty with Pondos, 1886; sec. nat. affairs dept., 1893; comd. forces in E. Griqualand, Boer War, 1899-1902 (depa., 2 meda. and 2 clasps); ditto and ch. mag., July, 1904; mem. of S. African native affairs comm., Sept., 1903, to Jan. 1905; holds rank of colonel in Cape colonial forces; ret., May, 1907; M.L.A. for Tembuland, 1908; mem. of S. African National Convention in connection with South Africa Bill, 1909; mem. of senate, Union of S. Africa, 1910-29; dir., war recruiting, Union of S. Africa and commissioner for returned soldiers, 1918-19.

STANLEY, SIR HERBERT JAMES, G.C.M.G. (1930), K.C.M.G. (1924), C.M.G. (1913).—B.1872; ed. at Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford (M.A.); priv. sec. to H.M. min. resident at Dresden and Coburg, and British vice-consul at Dresden, 1897-1902; ast. priv. sec. to first Lord of the Admiralty, 1906-1908; priv. sec. to Lord Pres. of the Coun., 1908-1910; priv. sec. to Viscount Gladstone, gov. gen. of Union of S. Africa, 1910; sec. to gov. gen., 1913; resident commr., Southern and Northern Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1915; Imperial sec. and acctnt. to high commr. for S. Africa, 1918; first gov. and commdr.-in-chief, N. Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1924; gov. of Ceylon, July, 1927; high commr. for the U.K. in the Union of S. Africa, 1931.

STANLEY, W. B., C.M.G. (1923), M.B.E. (1918), Barrister-at-Law, Gray's Inn, 1921.—Served with 1st Border regt. occupation of Crete, 1898; S. Africa, 1899-1900 (med. and 4 clasps); 2nd lieut., W. India regt., 1900; lieut., 1901; ag. adjt., 3rd W. India regt., Gambia expedit., 1901, (med. and clasp); ag. trav. commr., Gambia, May and June, 1901; trav. commr., Gambia, Aug., 1901; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to ag. gov., Gambia, Aug. to Oct., 1901; capt., 1903; passed course of survey, schl. of mil. eng., Chatham, 1905; resig. comm., 1906; capt., 3rd
Yorks regt., 1906; qualified in native language; dist. commnr., S. Leone, 1910; prov. commnr., May, 1920; ag. col. sec., S. Leone, on various occasions, 1918-20 and 1922-23; gov.'s dep. on several occasions.

STAPLES, JAMES WEBSTER.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., G.P.O., Oct., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; transf. to C.O., Mar., 1923.

STAPLEY, FRANK R.—B. 1895; mily. serv., Sept., 1914 to Dec., 1919; temp. clk., C.O., Apr., 1920; apptd. cler. offr., 4th July, 1922; higher grade cler. offr., 17th Feb., 1930.

STARK, WALTER JOHN KIRKPATRICK.—B. 1887; ed. Robert Gordon's Coll., Aberdeen, and at Aberdeen Univ. (M.A.), 1908; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1910; passed cadet, Aug., 1912; offr., cls. V, Dec., 1913; asst. contr., lab., Apr., 1914; dep. contr., lab. (offr., cls. IV), Jan., 1919; emigrn. agt., S.S. and F.M.S., Cocanada, Sept., 1920; supt., emigrn. depot, Negapatam, Mar., 1922; mag., July, 1922; offr., cls. III, Nov., 1922; 1st mag., Kuala Lumpur, Mar., 1924; offr., cls. II, Nov., 1927; dist. offr., Nov., 1927; mag., Ipoh, Oct., 1928; ag. dep. contr., lab., Malaya, Apr., 1931.

STARNES, CORTLANDT.—B. 1864; served in N.W. rebellion, 1886, as ag. adjutant, 65th Montreal; Inspr., R.N.W.M. Pol., 1st Mar., 1886; adjutant, 1891-97; supt., 1909; asst. commnr., 1st Dec., 1919; commnr., 1923.

STATHAM, HON. SIR CHARLES ERNEST, KT. BACH. (1926).—Mem., N.Z. parlt. since 1915; speaker since 1923.

STEAD, KINGSLEY WILLANS, O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1883; ed. at King Edward's, Birmingham; apptd., after open compet. exam., asst. in impl. cust., Cardiff, Mar., 1903; Harwich, Oct., 1906; asst. collr. of cust., Larnaca, Cyprus, dep. harbrmr. and tide surveyor, Apr., 1908; collr. of cust. and excise, Apr., 1910; passed prelim. exam. in modern Greek, June, 1910; regir. of trade marks, June, 1911; passed lower standard exam. in modern Greek, June, 1912; asst. cable censor, Aug., 1914; Apr., 1919; cable censor, May-July, 1919; pub. cust. of enemy property, Jan., 1919 to Mar., 1920; refugee commnr., Larnaca, May, 1919 to Apr., 1920; regir. of patents, Aug., 1920; ch. collr. of cust. and excise, Oct., 1921; inspr. of fisheries, 1921; Médaille de la Reconnaissance Française, 3rd cls., 1922; ag. commnr., Larnaca for various periods in 1922, 1923 and 1924; regir. of companies, July, 1922; ch. supt., Port of Larnaca, June, 1922; regir. of companies, July, 1922; regir. of Cyprus ships, Jan., 1923; regir. of Br. ships, Jan., 1923; dir. cust., excise, and trade, Palestine, July, 1924; ag. regir.-gen., Aug. to Dec., 1924; regir. trade marks and patents, Apr., 1928; ag. regir. companies and co-op. societies, Apr.-Dec., 1928.

STEAD, ROBERT J. C.—B. 1880; asst. gen. publicity agt., colonization dept., C.P.R., 1913; gen. publicity agt., colonization dept., C.P.R., 1917; dir. publicity, dept. of immigr. and colonization, Ottawa, 1919; has written several books.

STEDMAN, HUGH JOHN HARRY, O.B.E. (1929), M.I.C.E.—Ed. at Weymouth Coll. and trained at Royal Naval Depot, Portland; asst. engrnr., P.W.D., E. Africa Prot., 1905; ag. exec. engrnr., Kisumu, Mombasa, 1907; in charge, Thika rly. survey and constr., 1910-11; ag. exec. engrnr., Nairobi and Naivasha, 1912-16; seconded to 3rd batt., K.A.R., 1915 ("1914-15" Star, Br. War and Victory meda.); exec. engrnr., P.W.D., 1917; D.P.W., Zanzibar, 1925; Brilliant Star, Zanzibar, cls. III., March, 1928.

SWETTENHAM, SIR J. ALEXANDER, K.C.M.G. (1898), C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1846; ed. IV., Nov., 1920; ag. ast. supt., govt. monopolies and ast. prot. of Chinese, Malacca, June, 1921; ast. prot. Chinese, Spore, Sept., 1924; cls. III., Nov., 1925; prot. Chinese, Kedah, Dec., 1926; ag. prot. Chinese, Selangor and Pahang, June, 1929; ag. prot. Chinese, Perak, Mar., 1930; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1930.

SYMES, LIEUT.-COL. SIR GEORGE STEWART, K.B.E. (1928). C.M.G., D.S.O.—B. 1882; ed. Malvern Coll. and Sandhurst; ent. Army, 1900; serv. S. African War (Queen's med., 2 clasps); Aden, 1903-04 (desp., D.S.O.); attd., Egyptian Army, 1906 and Sudan govt., 1907; Blue Nile expedn., 1908 (med.); promoted major, 1915 and brevet lt.-col., 1917; A.D.C. to Sirdar and gov. gen. of the Sudan, 1906-07; ast. dir. of intelligence, 1908-12; pte. sec. and sec. gov.gen.'s coun. (Sudan), 1913-16; European War (3 times ment. in desps., meda., brevet lt.col.); attd., staff of high comsnr., Egypt, 1917-19; attd., miny. of int., Egypt, 1919-20; dist. gov. Palestine, Sept., 1920; ch. sec., 1926; admast. gov't., Palestine, July to Sept., 1925 and May to Sept., 1927; accredited rep. to mandates comsnr., 1928 and 1928; res. and commdr.in-ch., Aden, 1928; gov. and commdr.in-ch., Tanganyika Territory, 1931.

SYMONT, SIR JOSEPH HENRY, K.C.M.G. (1901), K.C.—B. 1846; mem. of H. of Assem., S. Australia, 1881-1887; atty.-gen., 1881; Q.C. 1881; representative to Aus. fed. conven., 1897-8, and chrmn. of its judiciary comttee.; pres. of fed. league of S. Aust.; pres. of Commonwealth league; senr. for S. Aust., Commonwealth parlt., 1901-1913; atty.-gen., C. of A., 1904-5; has ret. from politics.

SYMONTETTE, W. J.—B. 1878; pub. schl. teacher, 18th Apr., 1898; 4th divn. comsnr., 11th June, 1921; ag. ch. clk. recvr. gen. in treas., dept., 6th Nov., 1922; confirmed in appt., 4th Feb., 1924.

SYMONS, CLAUDE TREVINE.—B. 1879; B.A. Oxon., F.R.G.S.; vice-principal, govt. training coll., Ceylon, Aug., 1908; asst. govt. analyst, June, 1912; ag. govt. analyst, in addn. Dec., 1916; govt. analyst, June, 1919; ag. regisr., med. coll. in addn., May to Dec., 1922.

TACHE, JOSEPH DE LABROUQUE.—B. 1868; ed. St. Hyacinthe Sem. and Laval Univ.; notary public, 1881; priv. sec. to Hon. J. A. Chaplean, premier of Quebec, 1890-82; priv. sec. to lieut. gov. Angers, 1887-92; proprietor and editor of "Le Courier," St. Hyacinthe, 1902-14; mem. of prov. coun. of agric., 1890-91; unsuccessful candidate for H. of C., bye-elec. and g.e., 1904; apptd. King's printer of Canada, Mar., 1914; jt. librn. of parl., June, 1920.

TAINSH, LIEUT.-COL. JOSEPH RAMSAY, C.B.E. (1924), V.D.—Offr., loco. dept., Indian rly., 1896-1917; 2nd lieut., Volunteer Force, India, 1898; major, 1915; major, Indian Defence Force, 1916; capt. (temp. major), L.A.R.O., 2nd Apr., 1917; ch. mech. engr., Basra Light Rly., 3rd June, 1917; ag. ast. dir., works, Iraq, 4th July, 1917 to 13th Aug., 1917; ast. dir. of works, in charge of Basra Light Rly., 27th Sept., 1917; trans. to Rly. branch, R.E., 4th Oct., 1917; lieut.-col., 15th June, 1918; loco. supt., Basra divn. of rly., Jan., 1919; dep. dir. rly., Iraq, May, 1919; dep. loco. supt. combined system of rly., Baghdad, June, 1919; demob. with rank of lieut.-col., 3rd Sept., 1919; loco. supt., combined system, Nov., 1919; ag. dir., rly., 11th Dec., 1921.

TAIT, HUGH NIMMO.—B. 1888; ed. at Clifton and St. John's Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. Math. Tripos, Part I. and II.; 1st cls. Nat. Science Tripos, Part I.; apptd. after compet. exam., clk., chief sec.'s office, Ireland, Oct., 1911 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Mar., 1912; ag. 1st class clk., 20th July, 1917; on mil. service from 27th Sept. to 9th Dec., 1918; sec. to Rhodesian Comsm., 1919-20; prin., 1st Apr., 1920; ag. ast. sec., D.O., 4th Sept., 1929; ast. sec., 24th Jan., 1930.

TAIT, HORACE VIBERT.—B. 1887 ed. at Harrison Coll., Barbados; Island scholar, 1906; 3rd clsr. class B.A., 1909; M.A., 1917; educn. offr., educn. dept., B. Guiana, 1914; ag. 2nd ast. inspr. of schools, Oct., 1914, to Apr., 1915; June-Sept., 1915; July-Oct., 1916; ag. 3rd clsr. olk., educn. off., Jan.-Apr., 1917; ag. classical master, Queen's Coll., Apr.-July, 1917.

TANNER, COL. (Temp. Brig.-Gen.) WILLIAM ERNEST COLLINS, C.B. (1919), C.M.G. (1916), D.S.O. (1918).—B. 1875; lieut., Natal Carbineers, 1899; ent. Natal civ. serv., 1899; served S.A. War, 1899-1902 (Queen's med., 4 clasps, King's med., 2 clasps); lieut., dist. adjt., Natal Militia perm. staff, 1903; capt., 1903; dist. offr., ditto, 1904; sec., Natal defence comtce., 1905; served Natal native rebellion, 1906; med. with clasp; staff offr., hdqrs., Natal Militia, 1907; major, ditto, 1910; grad., Staff Coll., Camberley, 1910; major, Perm. Force (staff), Union Defence Forces, 1912; temp. lt.-col., 1914; brev. lt.-col., Perm. Force (staff), 1915; lt.-col. comdg. 2nd S.A. Infy., Union Imp. Serv. Cont. (Overseas), 1915; brig.-comdr. (temp. brig.-gen.), 8th Inf. Bde., 1917; bde.-comdr., S.A. Inf. Bde., 1918; ret. with rank of brig.-gen. in Imp. Army, 1919; served in Great War, 1914-18, G.S.W. Africa, 1914-15, Egypt, 1916, and France, 1916-18; wounded, Delville Wood; ment. in desps. six times; "1914-15" Star, Br. War Med., Victory Med., Croix d'Offr., Ordre de Leopold and Croix de Guerre (Belgium), Croix de Chevalier, Legion d'Honneur (France); dist. staff offr., No. 1 mily. dist., and O.C. base, Cape Town, 1919; ag. adjt.-gen., defence hdqrs., 1919; substantive lt.-col. (staff offr., 1st grade).
Permit. Force (staff), 1919; adjt.-gen. and temp. col., Nov., 1919; ag. comdt., S.A. Mil. Coll. and O.C., troops, Roberts Heights, 1920; O.C., Cape Peninsula garrison, 1921; substantive col., 1921; temp. brig.-gen., 1921; dist. staff offr., No. I mily. dist. (Cape), in addn. to other duties, 1921; posted S.A. Staff Corps, 1923; adjt.-gen., defence hqrs., 1925.

TAVERNER, Hon. William Burgoyne.—B. 1879; ed. Caversham pub. schl., N.Z.; entd. N.Z. parl., 1928; min. of rlys., min. of cust., and comsnr. of state forests, 1928-30; min. of pub. wks., since 1930, also min. of transport, 1930-31.

TAYLOR, Arthur Percy, M.C., 1914 (Mons.) Star.—B. 1892; ed. Colchester Royal Grammar Schl.; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1926; served with R.N.V.R., R.N.D., R.N.A.S. and R.A.F., 1914-19; severely wounded, 1917; asst. acctt., P.W.D., Gold Coast, Jan., 1920; asst. commdt., Northern Territories constab., Sept., 1920; transferred to Gold Coast pol. as asst. comsnr., pol., Nov., 1923; comsnr., pol. and in charge, C.I.D., 1926; seconded to Ashanti judiciary as ag. pol. mag., May, 1927; pol. mag., sup. ct., Gold Coast, June, 1928.

TAYLOR, Edward Archibald Thornton, B.A.—B. 1885; ed. Dover and Corpus Christi Colls., Cambridge (schol.); B.A., 1907 (2nd cls. class. tripos); asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, Mar., 1913; dist. comsnr., Oct., 1918; senr. asst. col. sec., 1921; ag. ch. asst. col. sec. and ag. clk. of couns. for various periods, 1922-26; ag. sec. for native affrs., 1925; sec., bd. of examrs., native languages, Apr., 1926; prin. asst. col. sec., Apr., 1928; ag. dep. col. sec., 1928-29; dep. ch. comsnr., Ashanti and N. Territories, Mar., 1930; ag. ch. comsnr., Oct., 1930.

TAYLOR, Edwin.—B. 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to C.O., Jan., 1901; served with I.Y. in S. African war, 1901-02 (medal and four clasps); re-apptd. to 2nd div., and assigned to B. of T., 1902; elk., P.W.D., B.C. Africa Prot., July, 1906; treas., asst., Uganda, Jan., 1909; asst. treas., civil admin., German East Africa (occupied territory), Jan., 1917; treas., Seychelles, May, 1919; dep. treas., Uganda, Apr., 1923; ag. treas., May 1923 to 1924; senr. asst. treas., Sierra Leone, Apr., 1925; ag. treas., in 1925, 1926, 1928 and 1929; title altered to dep. treas., Jan., 1930; mem. Freetown temp. munic. bd., Dec., 1926; pres. city coun., Freetown in addition, May, 1928; dep. treas., Hong Kong, June, 1930; treas., June, 1931.

TAYLOR, Ephraim Godman, I.S.O. (1929)—B. 1877; ed. Wesleyan (Boys) High Schl., Freetown; civ. serv. exam., 1893; temp. outdoor offr., cust., Nov., 1894; 2nd cls. offr., Mar., 1896; compet. exam. in acctng., May, 1902; 2nd olk., acctng. branch, treas., May, 1902; 1st olk., Dec., 1903; 2nd grade elk., Jan., 1913; 1st grade, Oct., 1913; ch. elk., Jan., 1915; ag. senr. asst. col. treas., May to Sept., 1919; staff supt., treas., Jan., 1921; African asst. treas., Jan., 1923; ag. acct., elec. light and power supply dept., Freetown, Feb. to Apr., 1928.

TAYLOR, Frank William, M.A.—B. 1887; ed. at Newbury Grammar School and Oxford, Non-Coll.; 3rd cls. hon., mod. hist., 1910; bd. of educn. certif. exam.; certif. in geog., 1911; asst. mast., Magdalen Coll. School, Brockley, 1911-14; jun. supt. of educn., N.P. Nigeria, June, 1914; seconded polit. dept., June to Nov., 1919; regraded supt., educn., 1920; late capt., 4th Batt. Oxfr. and Bucks. Lt. Infy. T.F.; served in the Northern Cameroons, Garua and Banyo, 1915-16, and attached to the 1st Training Centre, W.A.S.B., 1917-18; publications, "A Fulani Grammar" (1921), "Two Fulani Readers" (1921), "A Practical Hausa Grammar" (1923), "A Fulani-Hausa Phrase Book" (1926), "Empire Reading Charts" (1926), "A Fulani-Hausa Vocabulary" (1927), "Fulani Hausa Readings in the Native Scripts" (1927), "Genesis in Fulani" (1927), contributions to the African Soc'y., the Philological Soc'y. and "West Africa."

TAYLOR, Hon. George Edward.—B. 1878; ed. London and Toronto; called to the bar, Ont., 1902; practised in London and Moosejaw, Sask.; K.C., Jan., 1913; pres., Sask. Bar Assoc., 1917; just., ct. of King's Bench, Sask., Mar., 1918.

TAYLOR, George Wilson.—B. 1866; ed. in Toronto; apptd. to excise branch, inland revenue dept., 1888; engaged in spec. organization work, Quebec, 1898-1909; asst. sec., inland rev. dept., 1909; sec., ditto, 1913; asst. deputy min. and sec., 1915; asst. comsnr. of customs and asst. deputy minister of inland rev., Oct., 1919; comsnr., excise, Apr., 1927.

TAYLOR, Greville Power.—B. 1899; ed. Elstow Schl., Bedford, and H.M.S. "Worcester"; asst. dist. comsnr., Sierra Leone, March, 1925; dist. comsnr., Mar., 1931.

TAYLOR, J. A. M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), L.M. (Dub.), D.T.M. (L'pool).—Med. offr., Uganda, Oct., 1908; temp. capt., U.M.S., Oct., 1914 to Nov., 1917; asst. med. supt., cent. asylum, F.M.S., 1920; S.M.O., Uganda, Oct., 1920; ag. D.P.M.O., Uganda, Mar., 1921 to July, 1921 and July, 1922 to Mar., 1923; D.M.S.S., Zanzibar, Mar., 1923; 3rd cls. Order of Brilliant Star of Zanzibar, 1929.

TAYLOR, Robert Stanley, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.A., M.D., B.C., D.P.H. (Cantab.), Cert., S.T.M.—B. 1875; ed. Downing Coll., Cambridge; exhibr., Charing Cross Hosp., London; D.M.O., Cue, West Australia; M.O.H., Cue and M.O.H., Day Dawn, West Australia; M.O., Uganda, Sept., 1914; active serv., E.A. campaign and temp. capt., U.M.S., Oct., 1914 to Nov., 1916; S.M.O., Somaliland, May, 1922; P.M.O., Somaliland, July, 1925.

TAYLOR, Robert Walter, C.B.E. (1928), O.B.E. (1919).—B. 1883; ed. Emmanuel Schl. and King's Coll., London; elk. in crown ag'ts. office, 1903-1906; head acctnt., Somaliland, 1906; ag. mil. paymstr., Aug., 1907 to Jan., 1908; Somaliland expdn., 1908-1910 (G.A.S. medal and clasp); asst. treas., Uganda, 1910; asst. treas., Somaliland, Mar., 1914; treas., Somaliland, July, 1915; dep. treas., Tanganyika Territory, Feb., 1920; ag. treas., Dec., 1921, to Mar., 1922; treas., Tanganyika Territory, May, 1922; ag. ch. sec., Apr. to June, 1927; gov't. dep. 10th to 27th May, 1927; govt. dir., Nyanza Salt Mines, Ltd., Meat Rations Ltd. and Dar-es-Salaam and Dist. Elec. Supply Co., Ltd.

TAYLOR, S. F., Labour inspection offr., E. Africa Prot., Apl., 1919.

TELFER, Elizabeth Wilson.—B. 1895; headmistress, govt. girls' schl., Accra, Gold Coast, 1st Oct., 1924.

TEMPANY, Harold Augustin, D.Sc. (Lond.), F.I.C., F.C.S.—B. 1881; ed. privately and Univ. Coll., London; asst. gov. chemist, Leeward Is.; 1903; ag. gov't. chemist and supt. of agric., July to Dec., 1906, and Jan. to Nov., 1909; gov't. chemist and supt. of agric., Nov., 1909; J.P., Antigua, 1910; offl. mem. legis. coun.,
Antigua. Mar. to July, 1912; represented Leeward Is. at 3rd Internat. Congress of Trop. Agric., June, 1914, and at rubber and tropical products exhibtn., June-July, 1914; chmn. of trustees Antigua pub. library, 1916; mem., Antigua Defence Reserve, 1905 to 1916; dir. of agric., Mauritius, 1917; nominated M.L.C., Mauritius, May, 1917; mem., bd. of dirs., Mauritius Inst., Jan., 1918; reported on S. African sugar industry, 1917; organised govt. tobacco factory, 1920; sugar experiment station, 1921; agr. coll., 1923-24; dairy, 1923; prin., Mauritius Agril. Coll. in addn. to substantive appt., 1924; reported on local sugar industry, 1926; organising vice-pres., Mauritius agril. and indus. exhibtn., 1928; chmn. various comttes.; dir., agr., S.S. and F.M.S., Jan., 1929; pres., bd., R.B.I., Malaya, Apr., 1929; visited Java as del., 4th Pacific Sci. Cong., June, 1929; author of numerous papers and repts. on agrl. chem., cane sugar production, agrl. educn. and trop. agr.

TENISON, EDWARD HERON RYAN.—B. 1898; on mily. serv., Apr., 1917; cadet, Ceylon, Nov., 1921; attd., Kandy Kach., Dec., 1921; office ast., Anuradhapura kach., Feb., 1924; ditto, Badulla kach., June, 1923; ditto, Batticaloa kach., Nov., 1926; pol. mag., Matale, Dec., 1927; astt. govt. agt., Badulla, Jan., 1929.

TENNANT, MATTHEW PETTIGREW, A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1881; ed. Montrose Academy; ch. astt. engrnr., Jamaica govt. rly., 1905; ag. loco. supt., ditto, July, 1909 to Dec., 1910; ag. ch. engrnr., Mar.-Nov., 1913; senr. engr. inpgr., P.W.D., Jamaica, Apr., 1914; ag. astt. dir., P.W.D., Dec., 1918 to Sept., 1921; ag. dir. of pub. wks., July-Oct., 1920; exec. engrnr., Uganda, July, 1924.

TESTER, L. M.C.—B. 1891; ed. Harvey Schl., Folkestone and privately; London County and Westminster Bank, 1909; Bankers' Inst. final exam., 1912 (hons. in common law); war serv., 1915-18; treas. astt., Nigeria, 1919; astt. treas., 1926; ch. acct., P.W.D., 1930.

TETTEY, VICTOR ADOLPHUS, B.A. (Durham).—B. 1891; 2nd cls. teacher, Accra Training Coll., Gold Coast, 22nd Jan., 1915; ag. housemast., 10th Mar., 1919 to 8th Oct., 1919; ditto, 11th Jan., 1920; 1st cls. teacher and astt. headmast., 1st Apr., 1923; inspector, schools, 9th July, 1925.

TE WATER, CHARLES THEODORE.—B. 1887; ed. Normal Coll., Bedford Grammar Schl. and Cambridge, B.A., LL.B.; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, and mem. of Pretoria bar; repd. Pretoria (Cent.) in Union parl't., 1924-29; high comsnr. for the Union of S. Africa in London, 1929.

THACKER, RANSLEY SAMUEL.—B. 1891; ed. Choir Schl. of H.M. Chapels Royal, St. James', Dulwich Coll. and the London Schl. of Economics; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn, 1913; held various legal appts.; ch. just. and pol. mag., St. Vincent, Nov., 1930.

THATCHER, J.—Ed. at Bristol Gram. schl.; examr. of loan accts., audit dept., O.R.C., Jan., 1904; examr. of accts., ditto, July, 1904; prov. aud., O.F.S. Prov., Apr., 1912.

THEILER, SIR ARNOLD, K.C.M.G.—B. 1867; state dipl. as vety. surg., Switzerland, 1889; dr., med. vet., Berne, 1901; hon. assoc., R. Coll. Vety. Surgeons, 1908; C.M.G., 1907; K.C.M.G., 1914; D.Sc., Cape, 1911; D.Sc., Syracuse, 1923; D.Ph., Berne, 1923; D.V.Sc., S. Africa, 1925; came to S. Africa, 1892; dir., lymph farm, Johannesburg, 1893; vety. surg. to sany. bd. and mine sanitation dept., Johannes-

burg, 1894-96; sp. mission to Rhodesia on outbreak of rinderpest, 1896; govt. vety. surg. to Transvaal Republic, 1896-1900; vety. surg. to Transvaal State Arty., 1896; dir., bacteriological lab. and vaccine inst., S.A. Repub., 1898; govt. vety. bacteriologist, 1900; dir., vety. research, Union of S. Africa, 1910; dir., Lamiekhte research, 1919; dir., vety. educn. and research, 1920; dean of faculty of vety. sci. and prof. of infectious diseases, Union of S. Africa, 1920; sp. mission to Europe to represent Transvaal and Natal govt's. at Baden Baden, 1899; sp. mission to Rhodesia in connection with Rhodesian tick fever, 1902; repd. Transvaal govt. at 8th International Vety. Congress, Budapest, 1906, at 9th International Vety. Congress, The Hague, 1909, and at Pan African Vety. Congresses, Bloemfontein, 1902, Cape Town, 1906, Pretoria, 1909, and at World's Dairy Confce, Syracuse, 1923; ret.

THEODORÉ, HON. E. G.—B. 1884; M.L.A. for Woothakata, Queensland, Oct., 1909; M.L.A. for Chillagoe from 1912; dep. leader of the labour party, 1913; treas. and sec. for pub. wks. in Ryan may., June, 1915; premier of Queensland, 1919-26; mem., house of reps., C'wealth of Australia, 1927; treas., 1929-31.

THEUNISSEN, E. D.—Ast. supt. pol., Kenya, Nov., 1922.

THIBOU, CLEMENT GARRY.—Foreman of wks., P.W.D., Antigua, Mar., 1915; ast. town clk., St. Kitts, Apr., 1916; ag. supt. of pub. wks., Aug., 1916.

THOM, M. ST. C.—B. 1887; S. African constab., 1905-10; astt. supt. of police, E. Africa Prot., 1911; supt. pol., Kenya, Jan., 1921; dep. commr., pol. and prisons, Uganda, 1931.

THOMAS, A. MOSGRAVE, Barrister-at-Law.—Crown counsel, Kenya, Oct., 1920; pres., dist. ct., Cyprus, Nov., 1924; ag. judge, sup. ct., on various occasions, 1925-1928; 2nd puisne judge, Trinidad, May, 1929, re-transfd. to Cyprus as puisne judge, Dec., 1929; ag. ch. just. for various periods, 1930-31.

THOMAS, CHARLES CLIFFORD.—B. 1890; ed. Blundells; 2nd lieut., The Duke of Cornwall's Light Infy., 1909; India, 1914-15; Aden Field Force, Jan., 1915; Egyptian Expedy. Force, Jan., 1916-19; adjt., 1/4th D.C.L.I., 1917-19; ment. in desps.; Territorial Decoration; adjt., 4th D.C.L.I. (T.F.), 1919-24; pte. sec. to gov. of Seychelles and clk. to couns., 1925.

THOMAS, HAROLD BEKRN.—B. 1888; ed. Dover Coll.; C.P.R., engrn. dept., 1907; Uganda Prot. survy dept., 1911; senr. staff survr., 1915; capt., K. African Prot. Forces, German East Africa, 1917-18; dist. survr., Uganda, 1921; dep. dir., surveys, 1924; ag. dir., surveys, land offr. and commr. of mines, Feb.-Nov., 1924, Mar.-Nov., 1927 and July-Dec., 1929.

THOMAS, HUGH WHITELEGGE.—B. 1887; ed. Dean Close Schl., Cheltenham and Jesus Coll., Cambridge, B.A.; astt. dist. commr., Gold Coast Aug., 1913; ag. dist. commr. at various times, 1913-17; dist. commr., June, 1919; ag. astt. coll. sec., Oct., 1919; ag. commr., cent. prov., May to Aug., 1924; dep. prov. commr., May, 1926; ag. commr., W. prov., Apr., 1927 to Mar., 1928; dep. sec., for native affre., Apr., 1928.

THOMAS, Rt. Hon. James Henry, P.C. (1917), M.P., J.P., LL.D., Cambridge.—B. 1875; served as cleaner, fireman and driver, G.W.R.; has served in turn as organiser, astt. sec., gen. sec. and pres., Nat. Union of Blymen; gov. of Dulwich College; mem., Balfour mission to
America, 1917; M.P. for Derby since 1910; J.P., Surrey, 1920; S. of S. for Cols., 23rd Jan. to 7th Nov., 1924; Lord Privy Seal, 15th June, 1929; S. of S. for Dom. Affairs, 13th June, 1930; S. of S. for Dom. Affairs and for the Cols., 28th Aug., 1931; S. of S. for Dom. Affairs, 9th Nov., 1931; author of "When Labour Rules" and other works.

THOMAS, LESLIE ARDING.—B. 1891; pol. probt., S.S., Nov., 1910; asst. supt., pol., Sept., 1914; ch. pol. offr., P.W., Mar., 1921; dep. commr., pol., F.M.S., Sept., 1926; asst. sup't. pol., S.S., Oct., 1926; adjutant, S.S. pol., Nov., 1926; commdt., pol., depot, S.S. and ag. sup't. pol., Jan., 1928; ch. pol. offr., July, 1930.

THOMAS, SAMUEL JOYCE.—Ed. King's Coll., London; Inglis schl. and early English Text Soc'y. prizeman; assoc. (with distinc.) King's Coll., 1897; B.A., Lond., 1897; called to bar, Middle Temple, 1898; enlisted, 1915; commissioned, R.A.S.C. (M.T.), and attd. to R.G.A. (145th Siege Battery), France, Flanders, Italy; invalided, 1919; ch. just., St. Vincent, Oct., 1919; ag. col sec. and admtr., St. Vincent, Feb. to Dec., 1920, and on three subsequent occasions; thanked by S. of S. for index of laws, St. Vincent, 1921; mem., W. Indian et al. appl., 1921-23; 2nd puisne judge, Trinidad, Mar., 1923; chmn., oil and water bd., 1923; ag. atty.-gen., 1923; 1st puisne judge on various occasions, 1923-26, and in 1928; puisne judge, Kenya, 1929.

THOMAS, SIR THOMAS SHENTON WHITELEGG, K.C.M.G. (1931), C.M.G. (1929), O.B.E. (1919).—ed. at Leatherhead and Queen's Coll., Camb. (scholar); B.A., Hons., 1901; asst. dist. commr., E.A.P., Aug., 1909; 3rd ast. sec., Apr., 1911; sec. ast. sec., Apr., 1912; ag. ast. ch. sec., Aug.-Oct., 1913, Aug., 1916-Mar., 1917, and Apr., 1917-Jan., 1919; clk. to exec. and legis. couns., 1917-19; mem.
